title: Quiet-window ops cheatpad: week cadence, rollout calendar & release notes (Sep 2027)
content:
Context and intent:
This is a compact, operational-oriented cheatpad for conducting low-traffic (quiet-window) rollouts during the week of 2027-09-13. It combines a lightweight calendar, operator checklists for pre/during/post rollout, quick smoke-test recipes, an explicit rollback matrix, and a rough draft of the user-facing release notes.

Why this exists (short):
- Quiet-window launches reduce blast radius for features that impact routing, KV-caching, or runtime kernel selection.
- Provide a repeatable, minimal overhead checklist for small batch rollouts that still need clear telemetry gates and rollback triggers.
- Capture the current rollout decisions so on-call and PMs have concise context.

Week-at-a-glance (UTC):
- Mon 2027-09-13: Preflight + staging smoke run (09:00–12:00). Prep notes and final config pin in config repo.
- Tue 2027-09-14: Canary batch 1 (02:00–04:00) — 0.5% traffic via tagging policy, observability probes live.
- Wed 2027-09-15: Canary batch 2 (02:00–06:00) — escalate to 2% if metrics stable.
- Thu 2027-09-16: Soft ramp (off-peak windows 03:00–08:00) — 10% routing shift planned; manual human approval required.
- Fri 2027-09-17: Full availability toggle at business hours (14:00) OR rollback if any unresolved regressions persist.

Preflight checklist (owner: Aisha / release lead):
- [ ] Config pins created and reviewed: model-variant, quant-profile, batch-window-ms, region-routing-policy.
- [ ] All linked PRs merged and smoke build tagged (release/quiet-2027-09-13).
- [ ] Canary manifest uploaded to deployment service and validated (schema & checksum).
- [ ] Staging smoke suite green x3 across 3 different sequence-length seeds.
- [ ] E2E baseline traces captured and archived for comparison.
- [ ] Observability: sampling rules in place, alerts enabled for token-latency, 95th/99th, error-rate, and KV cache hit ratio.
- [ ] Pager rotation and on-call handoff message posted to #release-ops with links.
- [ ] Stakeholder heads-up email sent to CS/Trust/Legal (if applicable).

During rollout (ops on shift: Marco / Liam):
- Canary 1 start: confirm target routing percentage and observe for 15 minutes before issuing next step.
- Live checks (first 30 mins cadence: 5m):
  - 95th token-latency vs baseline (threshold: +30% unacceptable).
  - Error-rate (HTTP 5xx + model-timeouts) > 0.5% -> investigate/consider pause.
  - KV cache hit ratio drop > 10% -> cause analysis for cache warming logic.
  - Streaming health: check chunk-delivery time and dropped-streams.
- Automated canary tasks: prefix-warm cache job (see linked_artifacts PR) must run within first 10 minutes.
- If metrics stable at 30m, proceed to next batch. Otherwise, hold and triage.

Smoke-test recipes (manual quick runs):
- Short prompt latency: 10 x 8-token prompts, verify median latency, verify token-cost alignment.
- Long context: 3 x 8k prompt emulations to verify KV eviction & latency tail.
- Function/tool call emulation: 20 calls through the function-calling path, assert no schema regressions.
- Streaming test: 5 sessions with simulated intermittent network, verify stream resume behavior.
- Metric-level checks: run the smoke-assert script (ops/scripts/smoke-assert.sh) and paste short result summary to the rollout Slack thread.

Rollback matrix (quick):
- Trigger conditions (any one is sufficient):
  - 95th latency > baseline * 1.3 for > 15 minutes and error-rate trending up.
  - Error-rate > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Functional regression detected by smoke-tests (API contract or hallucination spike on eval set).
  - Customer-facing critical incidents reported by CS within 30 minutes.
- Fast rollback steps:
  - [ ] Disable routing shift policy, re-point traffic to previous model-variant.
  - [ ] Revoke the canary manifest via deployment service.
  - [ ] Trigger cache priming rollback job (if new cache layout introduced).
  - [ ] Open incident page and assign SRE + runtime engineers.

Post-release (owner: Priya / PM):
- [ ] 24-hour quiet-window review: collect 3x daily summaries and an initial postmortem if any gating conditions were hit.
- [ ] Draft internal release note (short): what changed, why, owner, risk, follow-ups.
- [ ] Draft public release blurb (if applicable) — short bullet with potential user-visible changes.
- [ ] Add tuned config knobs to Optimize backlog if any cost/latency tradeoffs were observed.

Draft internal release notes (for internal distribution) — DRAFT:
Title: runtime routing + cache layout tweak (quiet-window 2027-09-14)
What: small change to the model routing policy (added region-aware fallback priority) and subtle cache key layout change to improve cache locality for short-context requests.
Why: reduce cold-start token-latency and reduce cross-region egress for short prompts.
Owner: Aisha Patel (release lead), Marco Alvarez (SRE), Priya Singh (PM)
Impact/Risks:
- Expected: ~5–12% improvement median latency on short prompts in region-us-west1.
- Risk: temporary 5–10% drop in KV cache hit-ratio during first 30–60 minutes as old cache keys are evicted; monitoring in place.
- Mitigation: prefix-warm job, staged ramp, and immediate rollback path.
Follow-ups:
- Add a nightly cache-eviction dashboard to detect long-term degradation.
- Revisit kernel selection heuristics for long-context inference (work item in backlog).

Draft public release note (customer-facing):
- We rolled out an internal routing and cache optimization that reduces latency for short prompts in some regions. You should see faster response times on simple queries; no action required. If you notice higher latency, please contact support and include request examples.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Does the prefix-warm job sufficiently cover all hot prefixes used in the sample traffic? Need a quick validation run against production sampling logs. (ACTION: Marco)
- Can we add a brief canary variant that only affects control-plane metadata to test rollout plumbing without payload changes? (Discussion: runtime & infra)
- Confirm legal/compliance review is not needed for the routing change (Priya to confirm).

Slack rollout thread template (use this when starting canary):
[rollout] quiet-window | runtime-routing-v2 | canary-1 | owner=Aisha | 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% planned | smoke link: <url> | JIRA: RINF-2318

Notes to operators: keep logs concise in the thread, paste short metric snapshots (95th/99th latency, error-rate, cache-hit) and one sentence decision (proceed/hold/rollback).

Appendix: quick check commands (examples)
- curl -H 'x-feature:routing-v2' https://api.redwood.ai/health - check route response and headers.
- scripts/obs/p99-latency.sh --since 10m --filter routing-v2  # quick p99 snapshot
- ops/scripts/prefix-warm.sh --manifest manifests/quiet-2027-09-prefixes.json
